Domino's Made A $7 Pizza For One Person
candidates.description: The pizza industry is in a slump: Papa John's stock has fallen roughly 80% from its peak, Pizza Hut just sold for $2.7 billion, and Domino's — one of the best-performing stocks of the 2010s — snapped its long sales-growth streak. Domino's answer is its first-ever personal pizza, a $6.99 rectangular pie called "the Domino," shaped like the brand's own logo after 65 years. But the real reason behind it has almost nothing to do with pizza. We break down why Domino's thinks its biggest competitor isn't Pizza Hut or Papa John's, and what that says about how everyone's eating now. candidates.title: Every Major Bank Is Now Paying You To Spend
candidates.description: Every major bank is now paying you $10 just for spending $10 — sound too good to be true? Paze, the checkout wallet built by the banks behind Zelle, is running a $10 spend, $10 back promo that's let power users rack up $1,000 in free Dunkin', Sephora, and GNC gift cards. It's spread across TikTok and Reddit as an "infinite money glitch." We ran the marketing math on what it's actually costing the banks per new customer — and whether the return is worth it. Disney's TikTok Deal Isn't About Watching Movies
candidates.description: Disney and TikTok signed the first deal in TikTok's history that puts its videos on another platform. Fan-made shorts built from Pixar, Marvel and Star Wars footage will run inside Verts, the vertical video feed in the Disney+ app, with participating creators getting licensed access to assets from hundreds of Disney films and series. It's the successor to the $1 billion OpenAI licensing deal Disney announced in December and lost when Sora shut down in March.
